::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Where do I find out how a command/environment is defined?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/4327/where-do-i-find-out-how-a-command-environment-is-defined), asked by [Seamus](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/215/seamus) on TeX Stack Exchange (2010-10-20; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> Say I want to redefine the `itemize` environment, or make a modified version of it. I want to know how it is currently defined. Where do I find this information? If it's some particular package command, I can just look at the `.sty` file for that package, but if it's something more basic, I don't know where to look...
>
> Is there a reference manual of where all this stuff is explained? Or is there a file in the depths of my texmf tree I should poke around in?
:::

Reading source code is a great way to learn TeX programming but it's not for the weak of stomach.  If you just want to modify an environment you can try the <a href="http://www.ctan.org/tex-archive/help/Catalogue/entries/etoolbox.html">etoolbox package</a> or some of the other <a href="https://texfaq.org/FAQ-patch">answers on the TeX FAQ</a>.

Oh, and one more thing: `\show\cmd` in a TeX file will interrupt processing to tell you the definition of `\cmd`.
